liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Bobby sings an altered lyric about once playing for acid and now playing for Clive; Listener checked repeatedly on headphones and concludes Bob sings about playing for Clive, meaning Clive Davis, instead of acid [1][11][13][15]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Called very powerful and possibly among the best ever, despite a couple of vocal miscues [17]
- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer complains about Donna's vocals at the end of Deal, finding them painfully bad [18]
- **I Need A Miracle** (1 review): Reviewer praises it as a great version lasting about eleven minutes [17]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer says Stella Blue sounds like falling crystals, and is beautiful [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-01-11.sbd.miller.fix-102430.102446.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 191 min; rated 3.38/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: This version has a fixed He's Gone; pitch is improved but still not perfect [1]
- **gd79-01-11.gatto.kempka.308.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 184 min; rated 3.86/5 by 35 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the sound as decent [17]
- **gd1979-01-11.sbd.miller.102430.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 191 min; rated 3.33/5 by 9 [2]
- **gd1979-01-11.125493.aud.cooper.berger.flac24**: audience recording; 22 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Bobby's altered Jack Straw lyric mentions playing for Nassau, disputing another reviewer's claim about 'acid' [9]
- A large Steal Your Face banner hung behind the stage; fans shook it during the line in He's Gone [11]
- Reviewer was 14 and chaperoned at their first Dead show; a woman outside called them little DeadHeads [12]
- Opening with Sugaree and encoring with Casey Jones were uncommon for the band at that time [11]
- Reviewer says these Nassau shows were the band's return to the venue since the 1973 bust [15]
- Lists this Jack Straw with versions from 11-6-79, 8-20-80 and 9-9-87 as standouts, and calls it the best [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-01-11.sbd.miller.fix-102430.102446.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Cassette (Sony D5) [1]. Also: Soundboard source from tapes provided by David Young and Rich Rothenberg, with seamless disc changes [1]
- **gd79-01-11.gatto.kempka.308.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Keith Gatto; transferred by Keith Gatto, Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Nak 300's and Sony TC-158 [4]. Also: Reviewer's older brother taped all four shows, though not the uploaded versions; quality was okay, not great [15]
- **gd1979-01-11.sbd.miller.102430.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Cassette (Sony D5) [2]
- **gd1979-01-11.125493.aud.cooper.berger.flac24**: taped by Jim Cooper; transferred by Rob Berger; source: source: aud cassette master taped by Jim Cooper; sony ecm22p's > sony tc-158sd, dolby b; set I, end of II: TDK SA-C90's, set II: Maxell UDXLII-C90; nak… [3]
